briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East saw a significant escalation in the past 24 hours with Iran claiming ballistic missile strikes on a U.S. airbase in Jordan and targeting three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Simultaneously, U.S. and Saudi forces conducted joint airstrikes against Iran-backed militias in Iraq, reportedly killing 20 and injuring 32. This direct and proxy conflict underscores a rapidly deteriorating regional security landscape, with heightened military postures and active flashpoints across multiple theaters.

IRAN
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced it targeted a U.S. airbase and Central Command headquarters in Jordan with ballistic missiles, while also claiming to have "hit and stopped" three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz for ignoring warnings. U.S. CENTCOM confirmed missile launches but stated all were successfully intercepted, causing no damage or casualties, a claim also supported by Jordan's military which intercepted five missiles. Iran denied any connection to missile launches from other countries toward Saudi Arabia.

Iran is reportedly set to receive an initial shipment of 300-400 Chinese shoulder-fired air-defense missile launchers (QW-12 and FN-16) within weeks, valued at $60-70 million, to bolster its short-range air defense capabilities. Overland routes through Urumqi, China, and Pakistan are being considered for delivery. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister, Kazem Gharibabadi, stated that Iran rejected Oman's proposal for a 50-50 joint control of the Strait of Hormuz, insisting on full Iranian control of the entry route and a portion of the exit route. He warned that any European warship approaching the Strait would be considered a "legitimate target" and reiterated that the Strait would "never return to its pre-war state," with Iran prepared for war renewal if its demands are not met.

Previously, Iran reportedly prepared a symbolic ballistic missile attack on a Ukrainian Black Sea port in response to an attack on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea, though diplomatic efforts eased tensions. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spoke with his Ukrainian counterpart, Andrii Sybiha, who claimed the attack on the Iranian ship was unintentional and not aimed at escalation. Araghchi stated Iran does not seek escalation but deems any attack on its citizens or interests unacceptable and demands compensation. Iranian acting Defense Minister stated production lines are more active than ever. Iran's Deputy UN Ambassador reiterated that illegal U.S. and Israeli measures threaten regional and international peace.

On the domestic front, the body of IRGC Air Force Su-24MK pilot Martyr Brigadier General Majid Kazemi, involved in a March 2026 strike on the U.S. al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar, was returned to Shiraz. The governor's spokesperson stated that Bushehr airport was completely destroyed in recent attacks and needs to be rebuilt. Iranian Intelligence of the IRGC reportedly shot and killed Kurdish cultural activist Mehdi Tavakoli, his sister, and mother on the Baneh-Marivan road. Mahnam Navab Safavi (22, rapper) and other individuals (Ghaem Hosseini, Amirhossein Maleki, Ali Dashti, Shervin Bagheri) are facing execution sentences from courts in Isfahan.

ISRAEL
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) demolished an underground Hezbollah command center, described as a 55-meter-long tunnel with three rooms beneath a construction material factory, in the village of Haddatha within the buffer zone in southern Lebanon. Troops also located a pit with dozens of weapons including assault rifles, RPGs, and explosive devices. An Israeli military vehicle was damaged in southern Lebanon, with investigations ongoing into whether Hezbollah fire was responsible. IDF troops in the Ras al-Bayada area fired upon a suspect approaching them in a threatening manner, killing Shadi Hussayan al-Darwish.

In Gaza, the IDF killed Muhammad Khalil Muhammad Aslam, a platoon commander in Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ)'s elite forces, in Khan Younis. Aslam commanded a cell involved in abducting Israeli civilians on October 7, 2023, and was recently advancing attacks on troops and civilians. The IDF also demolished the Al-Muttaqin Mosque near the Al-Yarmouk stadium in central Gaza City and discovered rockets in northern Gaza capable of reaching central Israel, which were subsequently destroyed. A false alarm for rocket fire was reported in Nahal Oz.

An Israeli man in his 20s, a member of a civil defense squad, was arrested for participating in a settler rampage in Huwara in June, where he was seen in military uniform attacking Palestinians.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House, with Netanyahu calling it "one of the best conversations." They discussed Iran, agreeing on a shared goal to prevent Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Trump stated he doesn't need Netanyahu to inform him about "Pickaxe Mountain" (an alleged Iranian site) and threatened to "take out" it, as well as Iranian bridges and power plants, if no deal is reached. Defense Minister Katz claimed U.S. fighter jets are taking off from Israel for strikes in Iran, which Iran is aware of, and expressed Israel's eagerness to strike Iranian energy targets, but stated the U.S. is currently not approving such attacks. Katz also said the IDF is preparing to conquer another refugee camp.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF operations in the Gaza Strip included the killing of Muhammad Khalil Muhammad Aslam, a PIJ platoon commander involved in the October 7 abductions, in Khan Younis. The IDF also destroyed the Al-Muttaqin Mosque in central Gaza City and located rockets capable of reaching central Israel in northern Gaza, which were subsequently destroyed. Hamas is believed to retain a significant number of rockets.

In the West Bank, an Israeli man dressed in military uniform was arrested for attacking Palestinians during a settler rampage in Huwara in June. A senior UN official expressed alarm over the "rapidly deteriorating" situation in the occupied West Bank, denouncing escalating settler attacks, while the Palestinian Ambassador to the UN, Riyad Mansour, called for Israeli settlers to be disarmed.

Israel's Supreme Court issued an interim order freezing a new law that paused arrests of ultra-Orthodox deserters, a move condemned by former PM Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman.

LEBANON
The IDF continued operations in southern Lebanon, demolishing an underground Hezbollah command center and a 55-meter-long tunnel with three rooms beneath a construction material factory in Haddatha. Dozens of weapons, including assault rifles, RPGs, and explosive devices, were seized in the area. An Israeli military vehicle was damaged in southern Lebanon, with military investigating if Hezbollah fire was responsible. Israeli troops identified a suspect approaching them in a threatening manner in Ras al-Bayada, killing Shadi Hussayan al-Darwish after warning shots. An interceptor missile was mistakenly launched at Israeli artillery fire in southern Lebanon, an incident currently under investigation. Israeli artillery strikes were reported in Tel al-Nahas and Nabatiyeh al-Fawqa.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Joint U.S. and Saudi forces conducted precision airstrikes against Iran-backed militia targets in eastern Iraq, including logistical sites and weapons depots, in response to over 30 drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities and U.S. personnel over the past 72 hours. The Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), an umbrella organization of Iran-backed militias, reported at least 20 killed and 32 wounded in these attacks, which targeted bases in Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala, and Diyala. The PMF condemned these strikes as "terrorist attacks" and a violation of Iraq's sovereignty.

Following these attacks, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Saidi canceled his planned visit to Saudi Arabia and called for an urgent government meeting to discuss the security developments. Explosions were also reported near a U.S. base in Erbil, northern Iraq, possibly due to a drone attack. The U.S. Embassy in Baghdad reissued a warning advising American citizens against traveling to Iraq. Yemen's Ansarullah movement condemned the U.S.-Saudi aggression in Iraq and affirmed Iraq's right to respond.

A Saudi "Karial" reconnaissance drone was shot down over Sa'ada province in Yemen during "hostile activities," and Yemen's Houthis claimed to have targeted the Saudi oil tanker NCC Ghazal with ballistic missiles for violating a maritime blockade.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's Defense Ministry announced it intercepted several drones targeting oil facilities in the eastern province, blaming Iran-backed militias operating from Iraq and reserving the right to respond. Saudi Aramco reportedly shut down its Jazan oil refinery and sustained damage to its Yanbu facilities following Yemeni attacks. Yemen's Houthis also claimed to have targeted the Saudi oil tanker NCC Ghazal with ballistic missiles for violating a maritime navigation ban.

Oman presented a proposal for a Gulf-backed plan introducing voluntary transit fees for ships in the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to resolve maritime disruptions and ease tensions. However, this proposal was rejected by both Iran (which insists on full control) and the U.S. (which insists on free navigation). Several Gulf states reportedly support the Omani initiative, which excludes exclusive Iranian control and features voluntary payments.

The United Arab Emirates (UAE), previously a hardline opponent of Iran, is reportedly working to de-escalate tensions, recognizing geographical limitations and seeking to protect its status as a regional economic hub. Simultaneously, the UAE is expanding security cooperation with both Israel and the U.S. Saudi Arabia has remained silent on U.S. President Trump's condition for a nuclear deal, which includes joining the Abraham Accords. Kuwait's Foreign Minister discussed regional security and de-escalation with his Qatari counterpart. Qatar condemned former Israeli PM Naftali Bennett's call to designate it an enemy state, with Bennett accusing Qatar of funding Hamas and celebrating the October 7 massacre.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Direct Iran-US Military Engagement:** Iran's IRGC claimed to have launched ballistic missiles at a U.S. airbase and Central Command headquarters in Jordan and "hit and stopped" three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. CENTCOM confirmed missile launches but stated all were intercepted with no damage or casualties. Jordan also confirmed intercepting five missiles.
2.  **US-Saudi Joint Strikes in Iraq:** U.S. and Saudi forces conducted precision airstrikes targeting Iran-backed militia positions in eastern Iraq in response to over 30 drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities and U.S. personnel. Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) reported 20 killed and 32 wounded in these strikes.
3.  **Hormuz Control Dispute:** Iran rejected Oman's proposal for a 50-50 joint control of the Strait of Hormuz, asserting its intent for full Iranian control over the entry route and part of the exit route, threatening European warships and warning of war renewal if its demands are not met.
4.  **Iranian Air Defense Acquisition:** Iran is expected to receive 300-400 Chinese shoulder-fired air-defense missiles (QW-12 and FN-16) valued at $60-70 million within weeks to enhance its short-range air defense capabilities, potentially via overland routes through Pakistan.
5.  **Netanyahu-Trump Meeting:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House, discussing a shared objective to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Trump issued warnings to Iran regarding potential strikes on "Pickaxe Mountain" (an alleged Iranian site), bridges, and power plants if a deal is not reached.
6.  **IDF Operations in Lebanon and Gaza:** The IDF demolished an underground Hezbollah command center in Haddatha, southern Lebanon, and killed Muhammad Khalil Muhammad Aslam, a PIJ commander involved in the October 7 abductions, in Khan Younis, Gaza. An Israeli military vehicle was also damaged in southern Lebanon, and the Al-Muttaqin Mosque was demolished in Gaza City.
7.  **Iraqi Political Reaction:** Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Saidi canceled his planned visit to Saudi Arabia and convened an urgent government meeting following the U.S.-Saudi airstrikes, indicating a severe diplomatic and security fallout.
8.  **U.S. Sanctions on Russia and Iran:** The U.S. Senate advanced a bill (86-12), named after Lindsey Graham, to impose new sanctions on Russia and extend the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to 2031, aiming to increase economic pressure.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high following direct Iranian missile launches at a U.S. military base and alleged targeting of oil tankers, coupled with retaliatory U.S.-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias. The Strait of Hormuz remains an active flashpoint, with Iran’s explicit rejection of shared control and threats against European naval presence signaling potential maritime confrontations. Iraq has emerged as a major flashpoint, with significant casualties among Iran-backed groups leading to heightened calls for retaliation and a canceled high-level diplomatic visit.

Military postures indicate increased readiness; the U.S. military is on high alert, and Iranian sources declare full readiness for a comprehensive war, while actively acquiring advanced shoulder-fired air defense systems. Israeli Defense Minister Katz's statement about U.S. fighter jets operating from Israel for strikes in Iran, combined with Israel's stated eagerness to strike Iranian energy targets (despite U.S. non-approval), indicates potential for further expansion of combat zones.

Red lines are becoming clearer: Iran considers any attack on its citizens or interests unacceptable and views any European warship near Hormuz as a legitimate target. The U.S. has warned Iran and its proxies that continued attacks will result in further military action. The potential for miscalculation or unintended escalation across these flashpoints is substantial.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** confirmed the interception of Iranian missiles and warned Iran and its proxies to cease attacks or face further military action. President Trump indicated "good discussions" with Iran but reiterated threats against Iranian infrastructure (including "Pickaxe Mountain," bridges, and power plants) if a deal is not reached. The U.S. rejected Oman's proposal for shared control of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. Senate approved a bill to impose sanctions on Russia and extend sanctions on Iran, with Jay Clayton confirmed as the new Director of National Intelligence.

**Gulf States** reacted to the escalating situation: Saudi Arabia intercepted drones targeting its oil facilities, blaming Iran-backed militias, and reserved the right to respond. Saudi Aramco reportedly suffered damage and operational shutdowns due to Yemeni attacks. Oman's proposal for the Strait of Hormuz, supported by other Gulf states, was rejected by both Iran and the U.S. The UAE is reportedly shifting towards de-escalation with Iran while simultaneously deepening security cooperation with Israel and the U.S. Kuwait and Qatar's Foreign Ministers discussed regional security. Saudi Arabia has remained silent on Trump's condition for a nuclear deal involving the Abraham Accords.

**European** responses varied: EU Foreign Policy Chief Josep Borrell discussed the Gulf situation and Ukraine with Iran's Foreign Minister. However, Britain and France reportedly refused a U.S. request to join an international naval task force in the Strait of Hormuz, citing frustration over a lack of prior consultation from the Trump administration regarding attacks on Iran.

**Russia** warned that Ukraine's attack on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea should be considered an "attack on Iran itself," highlighting the importance of eliminating the "threat from Kyiv."

**China** denied Reuters reports of an imminent deal to supply Iran with shoulder-fired missile systems, labeling them "baseless."

**Ukraine's** President Zelensky met with President Trump to discuss, among other things, licenses for producing Patriot interceptor missiles. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha reassured his Iranian counterpart that the attack on the Iranian ship was unintentional and that Kyiv does not seek escalation.

**Yemen's** Ansarullah movement condemned the U.S.-Saudi aggression against Iraq and affirmed Iraq's right to respond. The Houthis claimed to have targeted a Saudi oil tanker with ballistic missiles and shot down a Saudi reconnaissance drone.

**Turkey's** President Erdogan continued a crackdown on opposition figures, including the mayor of Uskudar, Sinem Dedetaş, and her deputies, on corruption charges.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions emerged regarding military actions. The IRGC claimed to have "hit and stopped" three oil tankers and targeted a U.S. airbase in Jordan with ballistic missiles. However, U.S. CENTCOM and Jordan explicitly stated that all missiles were successfully intercepted, with no damage or casualties, indicating a clear divergence in reported outcomes. Similarly, initial reports on casualties from U.S.-Saudi strikes in Iraq varied from 8-12 killed among Iran-backed militias, later updated by PMF to 20 killed and 32 wounded, suggesting evolving or unconfirmed information.

The Israeli Defense Minister Katz's claim that U.S. fighter jets are taking off from Israeli bases for strikes in Iran, and that Iran is aware of this, is a major, unverified assertion that requires independent confirmation.

President Trump's repeated references to "Pickaxe Mountain" as an Iranian nuclear site he could "take out" lack corroboration from public information or other intelligence sources. This is further complicated by Israeli Chief of Public Diplomacy Tzipi Hotovely's statement that "Pickaxe Mountain" was "absolutely not" discussed in the Trump-Netanyahu meeting, raising questions about the specificity or accuracy of Trump's public remarks or whether it refers to a classified or misnamed location.

Several sources display clear propaganda indicators. The Omid Dana channel exhibits extreme anti-Shia and anti-Iran sentiment, openly celebrating casualties among Iraqi PMF and expressing wishes for attacks on holy sites, rendering its reporting highly biased. Statements from Iranian officials emphasizing "full control" over Hormuz and issuing threats against European vessels are designed to project strength and deter adversaries. Press TV consistently frames Iranian actions as "resistance" and U.S./Israeli actions as "aggression," while highlighting polls on low U.S. public support for war, aligning with state media narratives.

Reporting gaps include a lack of specific details on the identities or types of the "three oil tankers" allegedly hit by the IRGC, and no independent confirmation of any damage to them. Similarly, the precise targets within the "U.S. air base and Central Command headquarters" in Jordan were not detailed by Iranian sources. There were also unverified reports linking Melania Trump's absence from Lindsey Graham's funeral to Iranian terror threats. Both China and Pakistan denied involvement in the alleged transfer of Chinese shoulder-fired missile systems to Iran, as reported by Reuters.
